Zerya: Probably Kurdish or Turkish, possibly linked to Zerya/Zeryan meaning 'golden' or 'bright'. Origin uncertain.
Aliyana: Modern elaboration of Aliya, from Arabic 'exalted, sublime' (or Hebrew aliyah 'ascent'). Used across Muslim and Jewish communities.
Efsun: Turkish, meaning 'spell, charm, enchantment'. Used as a girls' name in Turkey.
Emima: Variant of Jemima, from Hebrew Yemimah, usually explained as 'dove'. One of Job's daughters in the Bible.
Hisham: Arabic, meaning 'generosity' or 'liberal giving'. Borne by several Umayyad caliphs.
Jaxon: Modern English spelling of Jackson, 'son of Jack'. Popular in recent decades, helped by the sound of the -x- ending.
Khadijah: Arabic, possibly meaning 'premature child'. Borne by the Prophet Muhammad's first wife and a revered figure in Islam.
Leif: Old Norse, meaning 'heir' or 'descendant'. Known from the Viking explorer Leif Erikson.
Maan: Arabic, meaning 'help, assistance' or 'one who provides'. Occasionally used for girls in the Low Countries; Dutch maan also means 'moon'.
Maisie: Scottish diminutive of Mairead (Margaret), from Greek margarites 'pearl'. Also used independently in English.
Manny: English short form of Manuel or Emmanuel, from Hebrew 'God is with us'.
Olli: Finnish and Nordic short form of Olavi (Olaf), from Old Norse 'ancestor's descendant'. Also a variant of Ollie.
Zala: Slovenian girls' name; probably from a Slavic word linked to 'green' or 'greenery'. Origin uncertain.
Ziyed: Variant of Arabic Ziyad, meaning 'increase, growth, abundance'. Common in North Africa.
Asael: Hebrew, meaning 'God has made'. Several biblical figures bear it, including David's nephew.
Emelia: Variant of Emilia, from Latin Aemilia, the Roman family name Aemilius, possibly 'rival' or 'industrious'.
Isai: Spanish and Hebrew form of Jesse, father of King David. Meaning is uncertain, possibly 'gift' or 'man'.
Julaybib: Arabic, a diminutive of jilbab 'garment'. Borne by a companion of the Prophet Muhammad.
Julôt: Probably a Walloon or French diminutive of Jules (Julius), from the Roman family name Julius. Rare; origin uncertain.
Maliyah: Modern American coinage, likely a variant of Aaliyah or Maliah; possibly from Hebrew Maliah 'God's wealth'. Origin uncertain.
Shekinah: Hebrew, meaning 'dwelling' or 'divine presence'. Refers to God's presence among people in Jewish tradition.
Til: Short form of Tilman or Till, Low German forms of Dietrich-type names, from Germanic 'people'. Also Till Eulenspiegel.
Uzair: Arabic, meaning 'helper' or 'strong'. Identified with the prophet Ezra in Islamic tradition.
Yeva: Ukrainian and Armenian form of Eve, from Hebrew Chavah, 'life' or 'living'.
Ahad: Arabic, meaning 'one, unique', one of the attributes of God. Also Hebrew-related Ahad Ha'am.
Diariou: West African, probably Fula (Guinea), a form of Diariou/Diaryou. Meaning uncertain.
Heitor: Portuguese form of Hector, from Greek 'holding fast'. The Trojan hero of Homer's Iliad.
Isaïe: French form of Isaiah, from Hebrew Yeshayahu, 'God is salvation'.
Soleil: French, meaning 'sun'. Used as a modern given name.
Affan: Arabic, derived from a root meaning 'chastity, purity'. Father of the caliph Uthman.
Amor: Latin and Spanish, meaning 'love'. As a boys' name it also occurs in Arabic-speaking North Africa with other meanings.
Bodi: Probably a short form of Bodo, Germanic 'messenger, commander'. Also used in Hungarian and Arabic contexts; origin uncertain.
Josée: French feminine of Joseph, from Hebrew 'God will add'.
Siar: Probably Kurdish or Arabic in origin; origin uncertain. Possibly related to 'traveller'.
Zerda: Probably Turkish or Kurdish; possibly from a word for 'golden' (zer). Origin uncertain.
Aksa: Arabic, from al-Aqsa, 'the farthest'. Refers to the mosque in Jerusalem; also a Turkish and Urdu girls' name.
Tasnîm: Arabic Tasnim, meaning 'a spring in Paradise'. Mentioned in the Qur'an.
Yazen: Arabic, probably a variant of Yazan, an ancient South Arabian name; possibly meaning 'calm' or 'dignified'. Uncertain.
Alita: Spanish and Latin-style name, possibly from Latin 'winged' (alata) or a form of Adelita. Popularised by the manga Alita; origin uncertain.
Edzio: Probably an Italian or Polish diminutive of Edward or Edmund. Rare; origin uncertain.
Maylonn: Modern coined name, probably a blend of May and Lon/Mylo. Origin uncertain.
Naëlio: Modern coined name, probably from Nael or Noël with an -io ending. Origin uncertain.
Revi: Probably a short form of Revital or Reuben, or a modern coinage. Origin uncertain.
Sansa: Made famous by Game of Thrones; probably a coinage by George R. R. Martin. Possibly related to Sancha.
Çois: Short form of François (French), from Latin Franciscus 'Frenchman'.
Éli: French form of Eli, from Hebrew 'ascent' or 'high'. The biblical priest of Shiloh.
Foss: English, from a place name meaning 'ditch, canal' (Old English foss, Latin fossa). Rare as a given name.
Noéh: Variant spelling of Noah, from Hebrew Noach, usually explained as 'rest' or 'comfort'.
Taïm: Probably Arabic, from a root meaning 'enslaved by love' (Tayyim). Origin uncertain.
Keyhan: Variant of Kayhan, Persian and Turkish for 'universe, world'.
Livay: Modern coined name, probably a variant of Levi or Livia. Origin uncertain.
Thélya: Modern coined name, possibly from Greek thelo 'to wish' or a variant of Thalia. Origin uncertain.
Aro: Probably a short form of Aaron or Arnold, or Basque, Armenian or Finnish in origin. Origin uncertain.
Eylin: Turkish spelling of Aylin, from 'moon halo'. Possibly also a variant of Eileen.
Meera: Indian, from Sanskrit meaning 'ocean' or 'saint'. Also the name of the poet-saint Mirabai.
Rafif: Arabic, meaning 'delicate, shimmering, graceful'. Also used for the rustling of leaves.
Malïa: Variant of Malia, Hawaiian form of Mary, or a modern coined name. Origin uncertain.
Naleya: Modern coined name, probably a blend of Nala and Aleya. Origin uncertain.
Olle: Swedish short form of Olof (Olaf), from Old Norse 'ancestor's descendant'.
Émil: French form of Emil, from Latin Aemilius, a Roman family name possibly meaning 'rival' or 'industrious'.
Ahil: Probably Arabic Ahil, meaning 'family' or 'people', or Tamil. Origin uncertain.
Aira: Probably Japanese, Finnish or Irish in origin; in Finnish it is a girls' name. Origin uncertain.
Lareen: Modern variant of Lorin or Lareena. Possibly from Arabic. Origin uncertain.
Miroslava: Slavic, from mir 'peace' or 'world' and slava 'glory'. Feminine of Miroslav.
Afia: Ghanaian Akan name for a girl born on Friday. Also Arabic Afiya, 'good health'.
Avyaan: Indian, probably from Sanskrit meaning 'bright, first ray of the sun'. Modern coinage.
Enar: Nordic variant of Einar, from Old Norse 'lone warrior'.
Maze: English word 'maze', or a short form of Mazen. Origin uncertain as a given name.
Muska: Pashto and Urdu, meaning 'smile'. A girls' name in Afghanistan and Pakistan.
Raha: Arabic and Persian, meaning 'relief, comfort, rest'.
Wil: Short form of Willem, Dutch form of William, from Germanic 'will' and 'helmet'.
Aryam: Possibly a variant of Aaryam or Maryam. Probably Arabic or Sanskrit; origin uncertain.
Aurelle: French feminine diminutive of Aurélie, from Latin aurum 'gold'.
Ayzal: Probably a modern variant of Aizel or Azal, perhaps Arabic. Origin uncertain.
Elim: Hebrew, meaning 'terebinths' or 'strong trees'. A biblical oasis stop of the Israelites.
Watine: Probably from a French surname or place name of Walloon origin. Origin uncertain.
Yvar: Scandinavian variant of Ivar, from Old Norse 'yew' and 'warrior' or 'bow-warrior'.
Éléanor: French variant of Eleanor, possibly from Provençal Aliénor, of uncertain origin; often linked to Helen 'torch'.
Amayra: Modern name, probably a variant of Amira 'princess' (Arabic) or Amaira. Origin uncertain.
Oleksandr: Ukrainian form of Alexander, from Greek 'defender of men'.
Tyliano: Modern coined name, perhaps from Tyler with an Italian ending. Origin uncertain.
Ysaac: Variant spelling of Isaac, from Hebrew Yitzchak, 'he will laugh'.
Amael: Breton, from Amaël, from Celtic words meaning 'prince'. Also a modern variant of Amaury.
Amarah: Arabic, from a root meaning 'life' or 'long-lived'. Also Igbo 'grace'.
Elyjah: Modern spelling of Elijah, from Hebrew Eliyahu, 'my God is Yahweh'.
Ezrah: Variant of Ezra, from Hebrew 'help'. The biblical scribe.
Isalia: Probably a modern blend of Isa and Alia, or a variant of Isaiah. Origin uncertain.
Natnael: Ethiopian and Eritrean form of Nathanael, from Hebrew 'God has given'.
Robbie: English diminutive of Robert, from Germanic 'bright fame'. Here given to girls.
Taj: Persian and Urdu, meaning 'crown'. Known from the Taj Mahal.
Vivé: Probably a variant of Vivi or Viviane, from Latin vivus 'alive'. Origin uncertain.
Loué: Probably a modern coinage, perhaps from French louer 'to praise'. Origin uncertain.
Zaviyar: Probably a variant of Xavier, from Basque etxe-berri 'new house', or of Arabic Zawiyar. Origin uncertain.
Cellou: West African, a Guinean (Fula) short form of Mamadou Cellou, from Arabic Abdul-related names. Origin uncertain.
Mathya: Variant of Matthias or Mathia, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Bitanya: Ethiopian (Amharic), meaning 'God's gift' or 'blessed'. Origin uncertain.
Eliyanah: Elaboration of Eliana, from Hebrew 'God has answered'.
Ossayd: Variant of Usaid or Ousseyd, Arabic diminutive of 'asad' lion. Borne by a companion of the Prophet.
Solomiia: Ukrainian form of Salome, from Hebrew shalom 'peace'.
Yostina: Coptic and Arabic form of Justina, from Latin 'just'.
Zélyana: Modern coined name, perhaps a blend of Zélie and Liana. Origin uncertain.
Bitania: Variant of Bitanya, Ethiopian for 'God's gift', or of Bethany, 'house of figs'. Uncertain.
Divora: Variant of Devorah or Deborah, Hebrew 'bee'.
Nomée: Probably a variant of Noémie (Naomi), Hebrew 'pleasantness'. Uncertain.
Novée: Modern coined name, probably from Latin novus 'new'. Origin uncertain.
Ousseyd: Variant of Usayd, Arabic diminutive of 'asad' lion. Borne by a companion of the Prophet.
Andrii: Ukrainian form of Andrew, from Greek andreios 'manly, brave'.
Lowenn: Breton, meaning 'joy' (Welsh llawen). Used in Brittany.
Lyle: Scottish, from a surname meaning 'from the island' (Old French l'isle).
Michiel: Dutch form of Michael, from Hebrew 'who is like God?'.
Silke: Low German diminutive of Cäcilia (Cecilia), from Latin 'blind', or of Sieglinde. Common in Flanders and Germany.
Jordy: English and Dutch pet form of Jordan, from Hebrew 'to flow down'. Also a Catalan Jordi form.
Maarten: Dutch form of Martin, from Latin Martinus, 'of Mars', the Roman war god.
Britt: Scandinavian short form of Birgitta, from Celtic 'exalted'. Also used independently in Dutch.
Stijn: Dutch short form of Augustijn or Kristijn, from Latin 'venerable' or 'Christian'.
Pieter: Dutch form of Peter, from Greek petros 'rock'.
Stef: Short form of Stefan or Stefaan, from Greek stephanos 'crown, garland'.
Yannick: Breton diminutive of Yann (John), from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Jérémy: French form of Jeremy, from Hebrew Yirmeyahu, 'God will exalt'.
Wouter: Dutch form of Walter, from Germanic 'ruler of the army'.
Brecht: Dutch short form of Albrecht, from Germanic 'noble' and 'bright'.
Kimberly: English, from the place name Kimberley, 'Cyneburg's clearing'. Popular after the South African city.
Delphine: French, from Latin Delphina, 'woman of Delphi' or linked to dolphin.
Nele: Low German and Dutch short form of Cornelia or Petronella, from Latin 'horn' or 'rock'.
Mélanie: French form of Melanie, from Greek melas 'black, dark'.
Jarno: Probably a Finnish form of Jarl or Jaroslav, or Dutch form of Jaro. Origin uncertain.
Kimberley: English, from the place name Kimberley, 'Cyneburg's clearing'.
Anke: Low German diminutive of Anna, from Hebrew Hannah, 'grace'.
Cassandra: Greek, from Kassandra, the Trojan prophetess; meaning often given as 'shining upon men' (uncertain).
Tine: Dutch short form of Martine, Katrien or Christine, from Latin 'Christian' or 'of Mars'.
Gitte: Danish short form of Birgitte, from Celtic 'exalted'.
Kenny: Scottish diminutive of Kenneth, from Gaelic 'handsome' or 'born of fire'.
Christophe: French form of Christopher, from Greek 'bearer of Christ'.
Evelien: Dutch form of Evelyn or Eveline, from Norman French Aveline, probably from Germanic avi 'desired'.
Caro: Short form of Caroline or Carolina, from Charles, Germanic 'free man'. Also Spanish and Italian 'dear'.
Lindsay: English and Scottish, from a surname meaning 'Lincoln's island' (Old English).
Maureen: Anglo-Irish form of Máirín, a diminutive of Mary. Hebrew origin, possibly 'beloved' or 'bitter'.
Mégane: French modern form of Megan, Welsh diminutive of Margaret, from Greek 'pearl'.
Axl: Variant of Axel, Scandinavian from Hebrew Absalom 'father of peace'. Made famous by Axl Rose.
Wendy: English name popularised by J. M. Barrie in Peter Pan, based on 'fwendy-wendy'. Also a short form of Gwendolen.
Kim: English short form of Kimberly, or Danish short form of Joachim. Also Vietnamese or Korean surname.
Gaëtan: French form of Gaetano, from Latin Caietanus, 'from Gaeta', an Italian town.
Stéphanie: French form of Stephanie, from Greek stephanos 'crown, garland'.
Alison: English, from the medieval pet form of Alice, from Germanic 'noble kind'.
Marieke: Dutch diminutive of Maria, from Hebrew Miriam, uncertain meaning.
Cynthia: Greek, 'from Mount Cynthus' in Delos, an epithet of Artemis.
Sharon: Hebrew, from Sharon, a fertile coastal plain in Israel, from 'plain, level land'.
Kilian: Irish, from Cillian, probably from ceallach 'bright-headed' or 'church'. Also German from the missionary saint.
Jente: Probably a Dutch variant of Jenthe, from Jan or Jente. Origin uncertain.
Martijn: Dutch form of Martin, from Latin Martinus, 'of Mars'.
Yarne: Probably a Dutch or Frisian coinage, perhaps linked to Jarne or Arne ('eagle'). Origin uncertain.
Gregory: English form of Greek Gregorios, 'watchful, alert'.
Frauke: Low German diminutive of Frau 'woman, lady', used as a girl's name in northern Germany.
Lobke: Dutch and Frisian diminutive of Lobbe or Lode, probably related to Lodewijk or Louise. Uncertain.
Caitlin: Anglicised Irish Caitlín, form of Catherine, from Greek 'pure'.
Maaike: Dutch and Frisian diminutive of Maria, from Hebrew Miriam.
Jeffrey: English, a form of Geoffrey, from Germanic 'peace' and 'pledge' or 'traveller'.
Marte: Scandinavian and Dutch short form of Martha or Martine, from Aramaic 'lady' or Latin 'of Mars'.
Madison: English, from a surname meaning 'son of Maud' or 'mighty in battle'. Popularised by the film Splash.
Giel: Dutch short form of Gilbert or Egidius, Germanic 'pledge, bright' or Greek 'young goat'.
Anne-Sophie: French compound of Anne (Hebrew 'grace') and Sophie (Greek 'wisdom').
Liese: Dutch and German short form of Elisabeth, from Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Perrine: French diminutive of Pierre, from Greek petros 'rock', via Petronilla.
Renzo: Italian short form of Lorenzo, from Latin Laurentius, 'from Laurentum' or 'laurel'.
Kjell: Scandinavian, from Old Norse ketill 'kettle, helmet'.
Kirsten: Scandinavian and Low German form of Christina, from Greek 'follower of Christ'.
Chelsey: English, a variant of Chelsea, from Old English 'landing place for chalk or limestone'.
Nicola: Italian male form of Nicholas, from Greek 'victory of the people'. In English also used for girls.
Kyllian: Variant of Killian, Irish 'little church' or 'bright-headed'.
Irem: Turkish, from Iram, a legendary garden or paradise mentioned in the Qur'an.
Merve: Turkish form of Marwa, a hill near Mecca; the name may mean 'quartz' or 'flint stone'.
Kyana: Modern name, possibly American, perhaps from Kiana (Hawaiian form of Diana). Origin uncertain.
Steve: English short form of Steven, from Greek stephanos 'crown, garland'.
Natacha: French form of Natasha, Russian from Latin natalis 'birthday', i.e. Christmas.
Marlies: Dutch and German blend of Maria and Elisabeth or Lies.
Thibaud: French form of Theobald, from Germanic 'people' and 'bold'.
Dieuwke: Frisian and Dutch diminutive of Dieuwer, from Germanic 'people' and 'protection'.
Maude: English and French form of Matilda, from Germanic 'might' and 'battle'.
Shirley: English, from a place name meaning 'bright clearing'. Popularised by a Brontë novel and Shirley Temple.
Magali: Occitan and French form of Magdalene, from Magdala, 'tower'.
Vicky: English short form of Victoria, from Latin victoria 'victory'.
Iben: Danish and Frisian short form of Isabel or Ibe, meaning perhaps 'God is my oath'. Here a boys' name; origin uncertain.
Valérie: French form of Valeria, from Latin valere 'to be strong, healthy'.
Chaimae: Arabic Shaymaa, 'beauty mark' or 'having a beauty spot'. Moroccan spelling.
Lieselot: Dutch compound of Liese and Lot, from Elisabeth and Charlotte.
Emelyne: Variant of Emeline or Emmeline, from Germanic amal 'work, industrious'.
Phaedra: Greek, from Phaidra, 'bright'. A figure in Greek myth, wife of Theseus.
Chaïma: Arabic Shaymaa, 'beauty mark' or 'having a beauty spot'. French spelling.
Keanu: Hawaiian, meaning 'the cool breeze' or 'cool mountain breeze'. Popularised by Keanu Reeves.
Phebe: Variant of Phoebe, from Greek phoibos 'bright, radiant'.
Shannon: Irish, from the River Shannon, perhaps 'old river' or 'wise one'.
